verdicts.reason: A shrinks the original into a tiny can, moves the SOLSTICE wordmark to an arbitrary, unreadable spot top-right, and stacks the body copy and CTA tight against the headline and the bottom edge. B keeps the logo centred over the can and the CTA gets slightly more room, but the can is still tiny, the logo is minuscule and the body copy sits jammed under the headline.

A actually re-lays out the design: a strong headline at the top and the can and CTA side by side underneath. But the body copy runs almost edge to edge, the can is pinned near the bottom-left edge, and the logo is microscopic. B is the shrunk copy with a misplaced tiny top-right logo, a cramped text stack and the CTA nearly touching the bottom edge.

A's two-column layout (can on the left, text panel on the right) suits the format and keeps a clear hierarchy, though the darker panel bleeds off the right edge, the body copy wraps into a narrow 4-line column and the logo is tiny. B is the same shrunk copy as before: the logo is stranded top-right, the type is crammed and there is no breathing room above the bottom edge.
